title: verbascum phlomoides var. nemorosum
intro: Verbascum phlomoides var. nemorosum, commonly known as woodland mullein, is a perennial plant species that belongs to the figwort family. It has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health issues, including respiratory problems, such as bronchitis and asthma, due to its potential health benefits of reducing inflammation and promoting relaxation. The plant's therapeutic actions are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which have been found to exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. The bioactive constituents of woodland mullein have been reported to possess anti-bacterial and anti-fungal activities, making it a potential candidate for the development of novel antimicrobial agents.
